 Print Friday OTT releases, November 20, 2026: 'Dhindora 2', 'Percy Jackson & the Olympians', and more movies, shows to watch online November is loaded with fresh picks for OTT viewers, with ‘Blade Runner 2099’ leading a lineup that covers Tamil romance, animated comedy, survival drama and a real-life documentary across Netflix, Prime Video, JioHotstar, ZEE5 and SonyLIV. Here are ten more titles to add to your watchlist this month. ‘ Haiku ’
 This Tamil romantic film follows Manohar (Aegan), whose possessive streak ends his first college romance suddenly. Years later, a fresh chance at love makes him face his old mistakes, and he slowly learns to drop his insecurities and choose maturity, healing and self-respect. Where to watch: Netflix Release Date: November 20 ‘Teen Tigada’
 An unplanned pregnancy shakes up the lives of aspiring cricketer Asmani (Prasanna Bisht) and musician Manas (Danesh Razvi). Just as career breaks appear, the couple must deal with approaching parenthood, family pressure and hard decisions. Where to watch: Zee5 Release Date: November 20 ‘ Percy Jackson & the Olympians ’ Season 3
 Based on Rick Riordan’s ‘The Titan’s Curse’, the new season sees Percy Jackson (Walker Scobell) set out on a risky mission to save Annabeth Chase (Leah Sava Jeffries) and free the goddess Artemis. With Kronos threatening Olympus, Percy and his allies must beat the clock to stop a looming disaster. Where to watch: JioHotstar Release Date: November 20 ‘ Dhindora 2 ’
 Titu Mama is back, now keen to clear his debts and repair ties with his in-laws. A treasure hunt with Babloo ji, Janki, Sameer and Bancho derails his plans and leads to chaos in the strictly traditional village of Kavita Mami (Sanjeeda Sheikh). Where to watch: Netflix Release Date: November 20 ‘Steps’
 This quirky animated fantasy comedy gives Cinderella’s story a twist. Lilith (Ali Wong), one of her stepsisters, steals the wand of the Fairy Godmother (Bette Midler) and accidentally throws the whole kingdom into confusion. Where to watch: Netflix Release Date: November 20 ‘Anbil Avan’
 Tired of the corporate grind, married couple Surya (Ashok Selvan) and Iyal (Preity Mukhundhan) move to a remote hill station to run a vintage homestay. Their peaceful plan falters when a powerful local threatens them and tries to drive them out, turning their new life into a fight to survive. Where to watch: SonyLIV Release Date: November 20 ‘Perfect Liars’
 Jude Derry (Irene Balmes) enters the prestigious Tagus University with a secret goal: to get close to the rich Cash brothers and uncover what led to her brother’s untimely death. As she goes deeper into their world, her hunt for revenge becomes a risky game of manipulation, seduction and betrayal. Where to watch: Amazon Prime Video Release Date: November 20 ‘Blade Runner 2099’
 Set 50 years after ‘Blade Runner 2049’, this sci-fi series unfolds in a dystopian Los Angeles ruled by bioengineered Replicants. Cora (Hunter Schafer) teams up with Olwen (Michelle Yeoh) to help her brother, and both must navigate a perilous world to find safety. Where to watch: Amazon Prime Video Release Date: November 25 ‘Primetime Preacher$’
 This documentary traces the rise of televangelism in 1980s America. It looks at the political clout and fierce rivalries of preachers Jim Bakker, Jerry Falwell and Jimmy Swaggart, and exposes the darker side of religion on television. Join conversation

 After her son causes a deadly bus accident, Vicentina (Rejane Faria) sets out to meet the affected families and apologise in person, while dealing with her own grief. Where to watch: Netflix Release Date: November 20 Poll Vote & Share your view 
 Do you prefer watching animated comedies or live-action dramas? Animated Comedies Live-Action Dramas 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion Which one should you watch first?
 Viewers who enjoy fantasy can begin with ‘Percy Jackson & the Olympians’, while sci-fi fans should mark November 25 for ‘Blade Runner 2099’. Those after a light laugh can pick ‘Dhindora 2’ or ‘Steps’, and anyone in the mood for tension has ‘Anbil Avan’ and ‘Perfect Liars’ waiting.
